title: Optical conductivity signature of Van Hove singularity in altermagnetic topological systems
authors: Fang Qin, Rui Chen, Xiao-Bin Qiang
abstract: We investigate the topological phases, joint density of states (JDOS), optical conductivities, and magneto-optical responses of a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting. The system hosts Dirac gaps at the high-symmetry points $Γ$, $\textrm{M}$, $\textrm{X}$, and $\textrm{Y}$. We show that the JDOS exhibits kinks at the corresponding Dirac gap frequencies and pronounced peaks at Van Hove singularities, whose positions can be tuned by the altermagnetic order. These features are reflected in the optical conductivities, with complementary signatures in their real and imaginary parts. Particularly, the Van Hove signatures in the transverse optical conductivity disappear in the absence of $d$-wave altermagnetism, revealing an altermagnet-induced optical signature of the Van Hove singularity. Finally, the Faraday and Kerr rotations inherit characteristic features of the optical conductivity. Our results establish optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy as sensitive probes of Dirac gaps and Van Hove singularities in altermagnetic topological systems.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how Van Hove singularities manifest in the optical conductivity of 2D $d$-wave altermagnetic topological materials. By analyzing the JDOS and $\sigma(\omega)$, the authors show that these singularities create distinct, measurable spectral peaks. This work establishes optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy as powerful tools for characterizing topological and magnetic order in novel quantum materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the optical conductivity signature arising from Van Hove singularities within altermagnetic topological systems.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the Van Hove singularity features in the optical conductivity are directly linked to the presence of $d$-wave altermagnetism, providing a unique spectroscopic fingerprint.
method: The analysis involves calculating the Joint Density of States (JDOS) and the optical conductivities ($\sigma(\omega)$) using theoretical models derived from the system's Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet incorporating spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting. It is characterized by topological phases and Dirac gaps at high-symmetry points.
key_observables: Joint Density of States (JDOS), optical conductivities ($	ext{Re}[\sigma_{xx}(\omega)]$, $	ext{Im}[\sigma_{xx}(\omega)]$), and magneto-optical responses (Faraday/Kerr rotations).
important_parameters: Altermagnetic order strength ($t_J$), Zeeman splitting ($\Delta_z$), and the frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The JDOS calculation is used to probe interband optical transitions, and the analysis relies on the Hamiltonian structure describing the altermagnetic order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure showing Dirac gap closures, the topological phase diagram showing Chern numbers, and the frequency dependence of the optical conductivities, highlighting peaks at Van Hove singularity frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the physical model (Hamiltonian), calculating the topological invariants (Chern number), determining the spectral features (JDOS), and finally mapping these features onto measurable transport quantities (optical conductivity).
why_interesting: The direct link established between magnetic order (altermagnetism), topological features (Dirac gaps), and measurable optical responses makes this highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter.
